definitions.explanation: The edge or side portion of a road. A somewhat technical, traffic-related term, most familiar in {路側帯|ろそくたい} (the marked strip along the road edge for pedestrians).

examples.japanese: {路側|ろそく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{止|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧。
examples.english: To stop the car at the roadside.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}→歩行者：03152_hokousha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{路側帯|ろそくたい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: Pedestrians walk in the roadside strip.

examples.japanese: {事故車|じこしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{路側|ろそく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{寄|よ}せられていた→寄せる：02329_yoseru⟧。
examples.english: The wrecked car had been pulled over to the roadside.

notes:
A traffic and road-engineering term for the side edge of a road. In ordinary conversation ⟦{道端|みちばた}→道端：28126_michibata⟧ is used instead; {路側|ろそく} appears mainly in fixed compounds and official contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {路側帯|ろそくたい}: roadside band — the lined strip at the road edge for pedestrians
- {路側|ろそく}⟦{駐車|ちゅうしゃ}→駐車：01466_chuusha⟧: roadside parking

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{道端|みちばた}→道端：28126_michibata⟧: roadside — the everyday, colloquial word
- ⟦{路肩|ろかた}→路肩：20701_rokata⟧: road shoulder — the unpaved or emergency strip beside the lane
